page.layout: One column of running text, with a running head and page number at the top right. The page is a single printed page, with no marginal notes and no catchword except a line at the foot.

main_text.p: ase[?] electorum oculos Deus illuminat, corda carnea seu mollia facit, mentes intelli-gentiæ luce illustrat.

Act.14.48. Gentes autem hæc audien-tes gauisæ sunt, & glorificabant sermonem Domini: & crediderunt quotquot erant ordinati ad vitam æternam. Non igitur crediderunt ad vitam non præordinati, ut iterum per Contrapositionem ratiocinemur.

2. Materia circa quam, seu obiectum fidei, est Euangelium Dei (quod antea per Prophetas suos in Scripturis sanctis) de Filio suo (facto ex semine Dauidis secundum carnem, declarato Filio Dei potenter secundum Spiritum sanctificationis, per resurrectionem a mortuis) nempe Iesu Christo Domino nostro. Rom.i.v i.2.3.

Verfatur itaque fides, qua iustificamur & viuimus, circa agnitionem & fiduciam Dei Redemptoris, Iesu Christi Immanuelis nostri, ac statuit eum esse nostram sapientiam, iusticiam, sanctificationem & redemptionem, &c. 1.Cor.1.30.
Porrò, fides non habet materiam ex qua: quia non est substantia, sed accides, seu qualitas infusa, & efficax forma, &c a-

page.notes: The first word of the page is partly cut off and uncertain, so it is marked [?]. The word "accides" may be "accidens" or "accidens" in another form; the printed form appears to read "accides". The catchword at the foot is partly unclear, and the mark at the left of the foot is probably a signature or stain, so I have not transcribed it as a signature. The reference "Rom.i.v i.2.3." is copied as it appears in the print and may be damaged.
